documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PRACTICE - MEDICATION FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 01/05/2022

Eight weeks on sertraline 50 mg. Mood noticeably better, sleeping through most nights, back to some walks. Mild nausea the first week, gone. No SI. PHQ-9 9 today, down from the low teens.

Assessment: MDD, single episode, moderate - responding.
Plan: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. She is stable enough for her PCP to continue prescribing; we are glad to see her again if mood slips or the dose needs rethinking.

cc: PCP

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mood follow-up, first since psychiatry handed sertraline back to us. Feels "most of the way back." Enjoying work again, sleeping okay. No side effects now. PHQ-9 7. No SI.
MS: tingling still drifts in and out, nothing new. Next neuro visit in May with a repeat MRI first.
Thyroid fine. Asthma: no albuterol since the winter cold.
Exam: bright, engaged. Lungs clear. Heart regular.
A/P: MDD single episode, moderate, improving on sertraline 50 - continue, we'll refill. RRMS per neurology. Hashimoto - continue 100 mcg, TSH at the physical. Back in the fall.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/16/2022

36-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting MS, Hashimoto thyroiditis, asthma and depression on sertraline (via psychiatry, now her PCP).

She continues to have intermittent numbness and tingling of the left arm and leg, coming and going without a clear pattern, and the right eye still blurs from time to time and then settles on its own.

Medications: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; albuterol HFA prn; sertraline 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with an autoimmune thyroid disease.

Exam: Acuity normal. Right relative afferent pupillary defect persists. Hyperreflexia of the left arm and leg. Left-hand intention tremor unchanged. Remainder of the exam as before.

Data: CBC, ESR and B12 all within normal limits. MRI brain with and without contrast 05/09/2022: multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

Impression: RRMS; exam stable compared with August.
Plan: Return in about six months or sooner with new symptoms.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36 yo, yearly visit.
Mood good on sertraline 50, PHQ-9 5. Work busy but manageable. Sleep fine.
MS: saw neurology in May, exam stable, repeat MRI unchanged pattern per their letter. Same on-and-off tingling. No falls.
Thyroid: no symptoms. Asthma: one inhaler a year.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen benign. No edema. Brisk reflexes on the left, as known; strength full; gait steady. Skin: no rashes.
A/P: Health maintenance - flu and bivalent COVID booster today. CMP, CBC, TSH. Pap due 2024. MDD in remission on sertraline - continue. RRMS - per neurology. Hashimoto - continue. Asthma - mild intermittent, controlled. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Neurology visit - diplopia
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP
Date of visit: 10/31/2022
Seen in urgent slot (covering for her usual neurologist).

36-year-old woman with established multiple sclerosis, seen in this clinic last year for left-sided numbness and right visual blurring. For one week she has had horizontal double vision, worse looking to the left, which disappears if she covers either eye. Over the last few months there has also been occasional tingling in the hands and feet. Previous right optic neuritis settled without treatment.

Medications: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, albuterol HFA prn, sertraline 50 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: mother Hashimoto thyroiditis; father depression; maternal aunt MS.

Exam: On leftward gaze the right eye fails to adduct, with nystagmus of the abducting left eye. Visual acuity 20/20 OD and OS. The other cranial nerves are normal. Sensation intact to all modalities. Reflexes increased in both lower limbs.

MRI brain with gadolinium 10/27/2022: multiple periventricular white matter lesions.

Impression: Right internuclear ophthalmoplegia - a relapse of her MS.
Plan: Follow up in this clinic; call if the diplopia worsens or new symptoms appear.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four-month check. The double vision she had at the end of October went away over the next few weeks without anything being done; she was driving again by late November. Some hand tingling here and there. Mood good, PHQ-9 4. Took a long holiday break. Thyroid fine.
Exam: eye movements full and conjugate today, no nystagmus that I can see. Lungs clear. Heart regular.
A/P: RRMS, recent INO relapse now resolved - neuro to follow. MDD on sertraline 50, doing well. Hashimoto stable. Next visit spring.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 05/03/2023

CC: Right leg weakness and numbness since this morning.

HPI: 37-year-old woman with MS and previous visual episodes. Woke this morning unable to lift the right leg properly, with numbness down the leg. Also a week of blurred vision in the left eye.
PMH: RRMS; previous optic neuritis years ago that cleared by itself; depression; Hashimoto thyroiditis; asthma. Pelvic ORIF 2019.
Home meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, albuterol HFA prn, sertraline 50 mg daily. NKDA.
Family: mother Hashimoto's, father depression, maternal aunt MS. Social: never smoker, social alcohol.

Exam: Right lower extremity strength 3/5 with reduced light-touch sensation. Other limbs full strength.

MRI brain with and without contrast: multiple periventricular lesions, some gadolinium-enhancing. LP performed; CSF oligoclonal bands present.

Assessment: Acute exacerbation of multiple sclerosis.
Disposition: Admitted to medicine with neurology consult for IV methylprednisolone.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/03/2023, discharged 05/08/2023.

Principal diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.

Course: Admitted from the ED with acute right leg weakness (3/5) and numbness and a week of left-eye blurring. MRI with enhancing periventricular lesions; CSF positive for oligoclonal bands. Received IV methylprednisolone 1,000 mg daily for five days. At the end of the course her symptoms had not improved: right leg remains weak and numb. Tolerated the steroids. Walking short distances with supervision; safe for discharge home.

Discharge medications: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; albuterol HFA prn. No new medications.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: Neurology clinic; PCP within 1-2 weeks.

cc: PCP, neurology

documents.title: Hospital records received

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen one week after discharge from the regional medical center (5/3-5/8) for an MS relapse: right leg weakness and numbness, enhancing lesions on MRI, oligoclonal bands on LP. Five days of IV methylprednisolone, no improvement by discharge.

Today: right leg still weak and numb, no better than at discharge. Getting around the house carefully, a friend drove her today. Left eye blur about the same. No fevers, no bladder trouble. Slept poorly on the steroids, now settling. Mood shaken but she is coping; no SI.

Exam: right leg weaker than the left, lifts it against gravity only; right leg light touch reduced. Lungs clear.

A/P: RRMS with acute relapse, not improved after IV steroids. Neurology appointment requested soonest, our office called theirs today. Work note for two weeks out, can extend. Continue current meds. Return to ED for new weakness, vision loss or fever.

37 yo yearly visit.
Since last: spring MS relapse with the admission; neurology following. Doing her job. Mood good, PHQ-9 4.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, albuterol prn. NKDA.
ROS: no chest pain or breathing trouble. Periods regular.
Exam: thyroid normal, lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft. No edema. Neuro: hyperreflexia, gait steady without a device.
A/P: Flu and updated COVID today. CMP, CBC, TSH, lipids. Pap/HPV next year. Continue everything. Follow-up 6 months.
